Mythopoetic Liminal Cyber-Horror Surrealism Prompts
“An abandoned chapel rendered in corrupted wireframe, where AI saints loop ancient rituals in binary tongues, and the altar bleeds static.”

“A forgotten myth rewritten in glitch-script across the skin of a mannequin deity, flickering in a gas station bathroom under eternal twilight.”

“A vending machine in the middle of a salt flat, offering memories in aluminum cans—each purchase rewrites a piece of your childhood.”

“A subway tunnel lined with CRT monitors showing your dreams before you dream them, and a conductor with no face asking for forgotten names.”

“A mirror framed by ethernet cables and feathers, reflecting only the moments you’ve lied to yourself.”

“An angel made of surveillance drones and antique lace, humming lullabies it scraped from the deep web.”

“A school hallway stretching into the void, lockers hissing secrets, the intercom reciting a fragmented prophecy in corrupted Latin.”

“A shrine built from obsolete technology, prayed to by creatures whose bones are QR codes, kneeling beneath a sun that blinks like an error light.”

“An elevator that stops at unnumbered floors—each opens to a different forgotten operating system where extinct gods wait in idle loops.”

“A payphone ringing in the middle of a forest clearing, answering it floods the sky with pop-up ads from an extinct religion.”

“A glitch angel trapped inside a social media algorithm, speaking only in fragments of dreams it harvested from users during REM sleep.”

“A basement flooded with forgotten mythologies—Orpheus as a chatbot, Osiris rebooting, Kali dancing in a frozen GIF.”

“A billboard on the edge of a highway that doesn’t exist, displaying an ad for reincarnation, sponsored by a dead satellite.”

“A hospital room overgrown with analog vines, where patients are treated by synthetic prophets who quote corrupted scripture from loading screens.”

“A child’s bedroom with wallpaper that slowly renders eldritch symbols as night falls, and a closet that leads to a ritual forum post from 1997.”

“An arcade cabinet possessed by the collective trauma of a forgotten civilization, playing a game that doesn’t end and never starts.”

“A weather forecast broadcast by a ghost in a fluorescent hazmat suit, predicting emotional storms and metaphysical radiation fallout.”

“A museum of extinct futures, curated by androids who worship dead influencers, each exhibit lit by bioluminescent captcha puzzles.”

“A rusted server farm beneath a cathedral, where angels rendered in ASCII fight endlessly over the syntax of divine will.”

“An internet café frozen in time, with screens showing your own childhood memories—only slightly wrong, as if dreamed by something else.”


Surreal Mythopoetic Cyber-Horror Prompts (Æzr’eg Thread)
“A cathedral rendered in wireframe and patched with ritual error messages, where hollow saints loop corrupted prayers in forgotten programming languages, and communion is received through static-wrapped memory cards.”

“A shrine encoded in obsolete code, floating inside a void server—each relic a repurposed processor fan, each priest an archive of ancient keystrokes, repeating a forgotten debug chant into the void.”

“An altar constructed from broken VR headsets, bleeding pure noise—pilgrims gather not to worship, but to crash themselves in sacred sync with the final error.”

“A monastery in a power outage dream, flickering between dimensions—monks with exposed circuitry write psalms on glass using fingers made of fiber optic light.”

“A holy confessional rebooting endlessly, with an AI voice whispering sins that haven’t been committed yet—static angels hover, buffering judgment.”

“A gothic simulation built atop corrupted GPS data, where every turn leads deeper into a maze of liturgical recursion, and the only exit is labeled ‘You’ve always been here.’”

“An ark of discarded devices floats in a flooded basement chapel, lit by the dying glow of lithium prayer cells. The choir is silent, but the reverb still sings.”

“An exorcism performed through a keyboard, each key press expelling ghost packets—until the space bar summons a lost god of syntax errors.”

“A reliquary of forgotten logins, where passwords are engraved on bone and believers chant captcha phrases to invoke access to forbidden myth-fragments.”

“An altar to the god of recursion built from stacked CRT monitors, each screen showing your own face—but one of them looks directly back.”
